find: Published Phase 2/3 clinical data shows tirzepatide achieving approximately 20–22% body weight reduction at highest doses versus 12–15% for semaglutide at equivalent dosing intensity. The ~7–9% differential is the subject of significant mechanistic research, with adipose GIPR signaling (particularly via cAMP/PKA suppression of lipogenesis) implicated as a key pathway.

The SUSTAIN program (semaglutide) and SURPASS program (tirzepatide) provide the primary published efficacy and safety datasets for these compounds. Key published findings from peer-reviewed literature:

MetricSemaglutide (2.4mg/wk)Tirzepatide (15mg/wk)
Body Weight Reduction~14.9% (STEP 1)~20.9% (SURMOUNT-1)
HbA1c Reduction~1.6%~2.0–2.3%
Responders >15% loss~37%~57%
GI Adverse Events~40%~40-44%

These are clinical endpoints in human subjects — not direct predictors of in vitro or preclinical outcomes. They do, however, validate the physiological relevance of the receptor mechanisms studied in preclinical research using these compounds.

CagriSema is Novo Nordisk’s fixed-ratio combination of cagrilintide and semaglutide in Phase 3 trials (REDEFINE program). Phase 2 data published in NEJM (2023) showed ~15.6% body weight reduction with CagriSema vs ~8% for cagrilintide alone and ~5.1% for semaglutide at matched doses — suggesting genuine additive or synergistic interaction.

find: Published Phase 2 data for retatrutide showed ~28.7% mean body weight reduction at 68 weeks — substantially exceeding tirzepatide (~22.5%) and semaglutide (~14.9%). The incremental effect above tirzepatide is largely attributed to GCGR activation. This makes GCGR contribution a high-value mechanistic research target, and retatrutide the only available research peptide that provides GCGR agonism in the context of full GLP-1/GIP co-activation.

The PRIME trial (tesamorelin for visceral adiposity) provides a key published dataset: 26-week treatment produced ~15% visceral adipose tissue reduction and significant IGF-1 elevation above baseline. For preclinical researchers studying visceral adipose metabolism, GH/IGF-1 axis modulation, or hepatic lipid effects, tesamorelin provides a sustained-stimulation model with a robust published clinical comparator.

Retatrutide (LY-3437943) is the most searched research peptide in the Houston area and nationally, driven by its triple agonist mechanism (GLP-1/GIP/glucagon receptor co-activation) and its published Phase 2 clinical data showing ~28.7% mean body weight reduction at 68 weeks — the highest recorded for any single compound in this class. As a GLP-1 class peptide researcher in Houston, Retatrutide is the essential third-generation comparator compound.
